title: Ink Stage — All-Hands Vision Manifesto
description: A single aspirational phrase commands an ink-black canvas with bone-white type scaled to the edge of discomfort — nothing competes. Unlike hero slides that layer sub-headlines or brand imagery, this one enforces silence as a deliberate design principle.
philosophy: This slide exists for the moment before strategy begins — when a leader stands in front of five hundred people and says the one thing the company believes. It refuses sub-headlines, supporting visuals, and decorative texture because each addition dilutes the gravitational pull of the words. The muted gold company mark is present but deferential; the message owns the room. It is built for speakers who trust silence and audiences who came to be moved, not informed.
goodFor: Company all-hands opening slide before the CEO takes the stage
Brand manifesto or vision-statement reveals at annual kickoffs
Post-rebrand or post-pivot cultural reset moments
Conference keynote openers where a single idea anchors the talk
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data context
Investor decks where financials and traction must share the frame
Training or instructional decks with step-by-step content
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a stage plunged into darkness the instant before a spotlight finds a single speaker — anticipatory, pressurized, and still. One phrase owns the entire canvas with the scale of a monument inscription, sized past conventional comfort so the words themselves become a physical presence rather than information to be read. The muted gold company mark signs the lower corner like a painter's initials — present but subordinate, never competing. Avoid gradients, surface texture, decorative flourishes, and any secondary typographic layer; the gravitational pull lives entirely in the tension between the phrase and the void surrounding it.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed ink canvas with no outer margin band — only a minimal edge clearance prevents the phrase from literal clipping. Single aspirational phrase spans a 12-column grid at full width with equal micro-gutters left and right; vertical placement sits at optical center, pulled fractionally above the mathematical midpoint so the words read as commanding rather than floating. Company mark pins bottom-left at a deferential scale with no accompanying rule, band, or secondary element. No header, no footer rule, no page number — structural silence is absolute.

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the same cathedral stillness as the title card but admits one quiet counterpoint — a single attribution or grounding phrase beneath the commanding statement, like a signature on a manifesto. The mood is monumental and unhurried; the composition breathes as if the room has gone silent mid-sentence. Asymmetric vertical weighting pulls focus upward, leaving the lower canvas as deliberate, pressurized void. Avoid illustration, iconography, texture overlays, or any list structure — the authority of this slide lives entirely in what is withheld.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; primary statement occupies cols 2–10, vertically anchored at roughly 40% from top so the lower canvas remains open void — hierarchy achieved through distance, not ornament. A single subordinate element (attribution, one-line kicker, or grounding phrase) sits below with a gap wide enough to read as intentional silence rather than spacing error. Scale contrast is the sole differentiator between the two text layers; no rule lines, icon clusters, or decorative bands are introduced. Muted brand mark or section tag anchors bottom-left at near-invisible weight; page number bottom-right — both recede completely from the primary statement.
